tier_rules.tier1: All 4 starter decks (each unique starter card once, 4 per class) plus the 20 most-seen non-starter cards per class.
tier_rules.tier2: All remaining class cards, all colourless cards (including the 4 tokens: Note, Flotsam, Gull Feather, Spear Tip) and the 5 statuses (dark art; they show up often in fights). Order: remaining commons, then statuses and tokens, then uncommons with colourless uncommons, then rares with colourless rares.
tier_rules.upgrades: Upgraded cards (e.g. Splash+) share their base card's art and are not listed separately.

meta.ranking_heuristic: Priority = global display rank, most-seen first, classes interleaved Tidecaller > Echo Mage > Cartographer > Duelist at every step. 1-16: the starter cards (basic attacks, then basic blocks, then each class's two signature cards). Tier 1 picks per class: score = rarity (common 100, uncommon 40, rare 10) + core card 10 + bridge card in 2+ archetypes 8 + enabler 12 (feeds the class engine: Surge/Recede/Tideturn; Resound/Sustain/Notes/Echo; any Waypoint, Chart, Expedition, Bearing; gaining Momentum, Parry, Bleed) + cheap (cost 0-1) 8, cost 3/X -8, conditional payoff (High/Low Tide:, Resound:, If..., Can only...) -6, + optional priority_boost from card_scenes.json. Picks are made greedily from whichever of the 3 archetypes has the fewest picks so far, so every archetype is represented (about 6-7 each); ties go to the higher score, then data order. Commons dominate because rewards are mostly commons and the Shoal Draft only offers basic and common cards. rank_score/rank_tags on each class card show the working.

art_spec.style: art/v2/style-guide.md: painterly dark-fantasy oil, coastal gothic, upper-left warm key light, cool upper-right rim, low-key values, one glowing accent in the class hue, subject centred with the focal point upper-middle and inside the central 80%, one oversized key feature, no text, letters, border or frame.
art_spec.prompt_suffix: dark fantasy oil painting, dramatic chiaroscuro, coastal gothic, muted desaturated palette, one glowing accent, highly detailed
art_spec.negative: text, letters, watermark, signature, logo, border, frame, card, ui, blurry, lowres, deformed, extra limbs, cartoon, flat vector
art_spec.class_rules: Duelist: long gold-guarded rapier in the right hand (viewer's left), short broad parrying dagger in the left; never mirror without checking. Use the class hero sprite as the reference image when the hero appears.

notes: Paths follow the Art Director's request (art/v2/cards/<id>.webp). Style guide §11 says cards/<class>-<card-id>.webp; the two disagree, so pick one and the path template here is a one-line change (ART_DIR / path in the script).

Card ids are used as-is. All ids are lowercase alphanumeric and unique across classes, colourless, statuses and curses, so they are filename-safe. They are short internal keys (e.g. undercur, exsang, cstrike) that can differ from the display name.

shares_art_with is used only for real duplicates; art_owner names the card whose painting a sharing card reuses (copy or alias the owner's file to the member's path). paintings_to_make excludes members.
Scenes are hand-written in tools/art/card_scenes.json. The card data is being tuned in parallel: rerun the script, and it warns about cards without a scene and scenes whose card is gone.
Act motifs (Tidewrack Act 1, Rust & Rivet Act 2, Stormglass Act 3, Pale & Gilt Final) appear where the card or its flavour points at a place; most class cards stay on the class motif.
